Every dashboard step is OWNER-performed; no credentials or private URLs enter the repo.

outputs: docs/RENDER_INTERNAL_WEB_DEPLOY_CHECKLIST.md (the single owner-executed checklist: numbered dashboard steps in dependency order - create service (repo, branch, root dir apps/web, runtime Node + exact version mechanism, build command, start command binding $PORT, plan with the Hobby/free spin-down tradeoff stated, region oregon for co-location, health posture), set web-service env vars BEFORE first build (INTERNAL_RULE_EVAL_ENABLED true-token, NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL=<owner-pasted private API URL - placeholder only>), then capture the new web origin and set API_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS on nycdf-api (exact origin, no wildcard, no trailing slash) + INTERNAL_RULE_EVAL_ENABLED on nycdf-api, the M5-T019 stale-flag-name check, the Blueprint Auto Sync = No confirmation, the honest exposure note (flag-on internal routes become reachable by anyone holding the API URL - unlisted is not secret-proof), the not-public posture (R004), the render.yaml nycdf-web restoration debt + duplicate-service caution (dashboard-created service is NOT Blueprint-managed), and an end-to-end owner verification script: load the web URL, flag-on surfaces render, resolve a real address against the live API, plus the expected-absent list (Supabase-gated features, B-001))

acceptance_scenarios.input: the checklist read top to bottom against the packet inputs
acceptance_scenarios.expected: every setting the owner needs is present with its exact value or an explicit <owner-fills> placeholder; steps are in dependency order (web env vars BEFORE first build because NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL is build-time inlined; the web origin exists BEFORE the CORS step on nycdf-api); both services' env changes covered; the Auto Sync = No confirm and the M5-T019 stale-flag-name check are folded in; nothing requires an agent to touch the dashboard (R003)

acceptance_scenarios.input: grep of the checklist + report for onrender.com hosts, real URLs, keys, or tokens
acceptance_scenarios.expected: zero real service URLs (placeholders only), zero credentials, zero secret names with values; the API URL appears only as <owner-pastes-private-API-URL>; D-043-R002 satisfied by construction

acceptance_scenarios.input: cross-check of every claimed name/value against the repo evidence
acceptance_scenarios.expected: flag name is exactly INTERNAL_RULE_EVAL_ENABLED with a documented true token; API_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS semantics match services/api/app/main.py (exact origins, wildcard rejected, unset = blocked); build/start commands match apps/web/package.json and bind $PORT; Node version matches CI (22) with the correct Render mechanism; every claim carries its source file reference

states plainly that the API has no auth and flag-on internal routes are reachable by anyone holding the API URL (unlisted != secret); internal/dev labeling stays; NOT a public launch - no listing/marketing/indexing steps anywhere (R004); the render.yaml restoration debt and duplicate-service caution are recorded as a follow-up owed, not performed here

risks: CORS omission bricks the deploy: the browser calls the API cross-origin and services/api/app/main.py blocks everything when API_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is unset - the checklist's step order must produce the web origin before the CORS entry
NEXT_PUBLIC inlining trap: an env var set AFTER the first build silently leaves the 127.0.0.1 default in the bundle - the checklist must sequence env-before-build and state the rebuild-on-change rule

turning INTERNAL_RULE_EVAL_ENABLED on for nycdf-api exposes the flag-gated routes to anyone holding the API URL (the API has no auth) - the checklist must say this honestly rather than imply secrecy (the directive's own words: not secret-proof)
Hobby workspace limits: free web services spin down after inactivity; the checklist must state the tradeoff and leave the plan choice to the owner
a dashboard-created service is NOT Blueprint-managed: the recorded render.yaml nycdf-web restoration debt must warn about a later duplicate-service collision instead of quietly conflicting
